newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-PEREZ SACKED, BIANCHI AND GALEONE UNDER PRESSURE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PEREZ SACKED, BIANCHI AND GALEONE UNDER PRESSURE.

text.p: Gregorio Perez became the first serie A coach to be sacked this season when struggling Italian club Cagliari dismissed him after yet another defeat.
The Italian news agency ANSA said on Monday the Uruguayan had received a telephone call from club chairman Massimo Cellino telling him his services were no longer required.
Perez, who had spent only a few months with the club, was expected to be replaced by veteran coach Carlo Mazzone, formerly of AS Roma, Ascoli and Cagliari.
Perez was among a trio of coaches to find themselves in the serie A firing line this week, with Carlos Bianchi of Roma, and Giovanni Galeone of Perugia also under pressure.
Cagliari have won just one of their six league matches and are third from bottom with four points.

Cellino's patience ran out after Cagliari lost 2-1 away to Lazio on Sunday. The Rome club played with just 10 men for all but four minutes of the match after Lazio goalkeeper Luca Marchegiani was sent off.
Bianchi of Roma was another Latin American coach to feel the heat after his team were beaten 2-1 at bottom club Verona.
Ten days ago Roma sprang one of the surprises of the season when they beat champions AC Milan 3-0.

For Roma fans who had waited more than a decade for a league win against Milan and who last celebrated an Italian title victory 13 years ago, it seemed that the good times were just around the corner.
But Sunday's defeat plus a 3-0 loss at Karlsruhe in a UEFA Cup tie in Germany last week may have dampened such enthusiasm.
Already eliminated from the Italian Cup and with a difficult task ahead of them in the second leg of their UEFA tie, Roma are sudddenly in trouble.
Bianchi has come in for much media and fan criticism for the manner in which he has changed his side, in particular for leaving out strikers Francesco Totti and Argentine Abel against Karlsruhe.
Fans have also been critical of Roma's Argentine defender, Roberto Trotta, a player whom Bianchi insisted on importing from Velez Sarsfield.
In Verona on Sunday some Roma fans displayed a banner reading, "Go Away Trotta".
Galeone, of newly promoted Perugia, is also under pressure this week even, though his side keep on winning.
Galeone and the Perugia owner, Luciano Gaucci have been at daggers drawn since a blazing row during a pre-season friendly tournament in Spain.
The tension seemed to be getting to Galeone last week when he went into hospital with suspected heart problems.
Out of hospital on Sunday and under doctors' orders to give up smoking, Galeone saw his side win 2-1 at Parma.
Perugia now have nine points, just four fewer than league leaders Juventus. But even that good standing does not appear to entirely convince owner Gaucci.
"I got cross before when we didn't pick up the points we ought to have but now I don't see any reason to be angry or bring in reinforcements.
"However, let's not fool ourselves, I'm waiting to see how we go against Udinese in our next match."
